patch_description:
This approach keeps the input graph as the starting state, repairs it by deleting edges that participate in the largest number of current common-neighbor violations, then performs degree-balanced C4-safe saturation.

After obtaining a maximal C4-free graph, it applies several small edge-exchange perturbations: delete a few strategically chosen high-degree edges, greedily refill using randomized balanced ordering, and retain the best valid result. Every candidate is explicitly repaired/verified using the common-neighbor characterization before it can be returned.

Unlike the original one-pass repair and fixed lexicographic augmentation, this uses global violation scores and local search around the input-derived graph, which should provide more consistent improvements across different input matrices.
